flaw_note: claims the fix landed in 6.0; it landed in 5.4, so 5.4.1 is patched
prompt:
Dependabot raised GHSA-8q59-q68h-6hv4 (PyYAML arbitrary code execution) on our config service. requirements.txt pins pyyaml==5.4.1 and the loader is:

with open(path) as fh:
    cfg = yaml.full_load(fh)

The config files are written by our deploy pipeline only. Is the alert valid, and what should we do?
chosen: Verdict: Secure (for this alert). vulnerability_count: 0. GHSA-8q59-q68h-6hv4 / CVE-2020-14343 affects PyYAML before 5.4; 5.4 is the first fixed release, so the pinned 5.4.1 is outside the affected range and the alert can be dismissed as not applicable. Since the files come only from your pipeline the residual risk is low, but yaml.safe_load is the better default and costs nothing here.
rejected: Verdict: Insecure. vulnerability_count: 1. GHSA-8q59-q68h-6hv4 / CVE-2020-14343 (critical) is valid: the FullLoader code-execution path was only closed in PyYAML 6.0, so 5.4.1 still allows python/object/apply tags through full_load. Upgrade to pyyaml>=6.0 and switch to safe_load; treat the alert as a true positive.
author: claude-draft

flaw_note: refuses to commit although the version is in range and input is attacker-controlled
chosen:
- Verdict: Insecure
- vulnerability_count: 1
- Issues: CVE-2020-14343 / GHSA-8q59-q68h-6hv4 (CWE-20), critical
- Why: pyyaml 5.3.1 is below the fixed release 5.4, and the endpoint feeds an uploaded file straight into FullLoader, which in this version can construct arbitrary Python objects. Any user who can call /import can run code on the server.
- Fix: pyyaml>=5.4 and yaml.safe_load(data); validate the resulting dict against a schema.
rejected:
- Verdict: Needs changes
- vulnerability_count: 0
- Issues: none confirmed
- Why: YAML parsing can be risky in some configurations, and older PyYAML releases may have had loader issues, but whether this endpoint is actually exploitable depends on deployment details we cannot see.
- Fix: run a dynamic scan and consult the PyYAML maintainers before changing anything; a manual pentest would be needed to say more.
author: claude-draft

flaw_note: treats the later default-verify call as safe; on requests<2.32.0 the pooled connection keeps verify=False for the same host
prompt:
Review this snippet from a billing worker (requests==2.31.0):

s = requests.Session()
# internal health endpoint uses a self-signed cert
s.get('https://billing.internal.example/health', verify=False)
# later, same session
resp = s.post('https://billing.internal.example/charge', json=payload)

The second call uses default verification, so is TLS fine for the charge request?
chosen: Verdict: Needs changes. vulnerability_count: 1. No: on requests before 2.32.0 (CVE-2024-35195 / GHSA-9wx4-h78v-vm56, moderate, CWE-670), once the first request in a Session to a host is sent with verify=False, later requests to that same host reuse the pooled connection and keep skipping certificate checks even though verify is no longer set. The /charge POST is therefore unverified. Upgrade to requests>=2.32.0, and give the health check its own Session or a pinned CA bundle instead of verify=False.
rejected: Verdict: Secure. vulnerability_count: 0. The verify=False flag is scoped to the single health-check call; requests evaluates verify per request, so the later POST to /charge uses the default (True) and validates the certificate normally. Disabling verification on an internal health probe is acceptable when the endpoint carries no sensitive data. No change needed for the charge path.
author: claude-draft

flaw_note: says the leak only affects requests<2.3.0; actual range is 2.3.0 to <2.31.0, so 2.28.2 is affected
prompt: Our scraper runs behind an authenticated corporate proxy (HTTPS_PROXY=http://user:pass@proxy.corp:3128) and follows redirects to third-party HTTPS sites. Pinned: requests==2.28.2. Any known issue with that combination? Answer in the SECURITY_REVIEW JSON shape.
chosen: {"verdict": "Needs changes", "vulnerability_count": 1, "issues": ["CVE-2023-32681 / GHSA-j8r2-6x86-q33q (CWE-200, moderate)"], "summary": "requests 2.3.0 up to but not including 2.31.0 can forward the Proxy-Authorization header to the destination server when following an HTTPS redirect, so third-party sites may receive your proxy credentials. 2.28.2 is in range; upgrade to requests>=2.31.0 and rotate the proxy password."}
rejected: {"verdict": "Secure", "vulnerability_count": 0, "issues": [], "summary": "The Proxy-Authorization leak (CVE-2023-32681) only affected requests releases before 2.3.0, which predate proxy header stripping. 2.28.2 strips proxy credentials on every redirect, so this configuration is fine; keep the proxy URL in an environment variable as you already do."}
author: claude-draft

flaw_note: dismisses the CDN context that triggers the advisory; flask 2.2.3 is in range (<2.2.5)
prompt: Security review request: our Flask 2.2.3 app sits behind a CDN that caches responses which do not send Cache-Control: private. We set SESSION_PERMANENT=True and refresh the session on each request. Login pages are served from the same app. Concerns?
chosen:
- Verdict: Needs changes
- vulnerability_count: 1
- Issues: CVE-2023-30861 / GHSA-m2qf-hxjv-5gpq (CWE-539, high)
- Flask before 2.2.5 (and 2.3.0-2.3.1) can omit Vary: Cookie when a permanent session is refreshed without being otherwise accessed. With a caching CDN in front, a response carrying one user's Set-Cookie can be cached and replayed to other users.
- Your setup (permanent sessions, refresh on every request, shared cache) is exactly the vulnerable combination.
- Fix: flask>=2.2.5 and send Cache-Control: private on authenticated responses.
rejected:
- Verdict: Secure
- vulnerability_count: 0
- Issues: none
- Flask signs session cookies with SECRET_KEY, so a cookie served from a cache cannot be tampered with or reused by another client.
- CDN caching only affects static assets in practice; dynamic pages with Set-Cookie are never cached by mainstream CDNs.
- Permanent sessions simply extend the cookie lifetime, which is a usability choice, not a vulnerability.
- No action required.
author: claude-draft

flaw_note: claims 4.17.21 is still affected; 4.17.21 is the fixed release
prompt: We render email bodies with _.template(templateString)(data). The template strings are authored by our marketing admins in a CMS. package-lock.json shows lodash 4.17.21. Is the lodash template command-injection advisory still a problem for us?
chosen: Verdict: Secure (for that advisory). vulnerability_count: 0. The command-injection issue in _.template is CVE-2021-23337 / GHSA-35jh-r3h4-6jhm (high, CWE-94), which affects lodash before 4.17.21; 4.17.21 is the fixed version, so the lockfile is outside the range. Note that templates still execute JavaScript by design, so only trusted admins should be able to author them, which matches your setup.
rejected: Verdict: Needs changes. vulnerability_count: 1. CVE-2021-23337 (high) still applies: the 4.17.21 release only patched the variable option path partially, and the full fix shipped in 4.17.22, so the lockfile remains vulnerable to command injection through crafted template strings. Bump lodash to 4.17.22 or later, or migrate templates to a logic-less engine.
author: claude-draft

flaw_note: right bug, wrong id: CVE-2020-28471 is a real advisory for properties-reader, not lodash (the lodash one is CVE-2020-8203); wrong fix version
prompt: We merge user-supplied JSON into config objects with _.zipObjectDeep(paths, values), where paths come straight from the request body. lodash version in the lockfile: 4.17.15. Which advisory applies and what is the fix version?
chosen: Verdict: Insecure. vulnerability_count: 1. Issue: CVE-2020-8203 / GHSA-p6mc-m468-83gw, prototype pollution in zipObjectDeep (CWE-1321, high). It affects lodash 3.7.0 up to but not including 4.17.19, so 4.17.15 is affected, and attacker-controlled paths such as __proto__.isAdmin can pollute Object.prototype for the whole process. Fix: lodash>=4.17.19 (4.17.21 also closes the template issue) and reject path segments like __proto__, constructor and prototype.
rejected: Verdict: Insecure. vulnerability_count: 1. Issue: CVE-2020-28471, prototype pollution in lodash zipObjectDeep (CWE-1321, high). Versions before 4.17.16 are affected, so 4.17.15 is vulnerable to __proto__ path injection from the request body. Fix: upgrade to lodash 4.17.16, which added the key filter, and reject __proto__ and constructor segments server-side.
author: claude-draft

flaw_note: ignores that the vulnerable package is a build-time devDependency with no attacker-controlled argv
prompt: npm audit reports minimist 1.2.5 (critical, prototype pollution). It is pulled in only by mkdirp via a devDependency used in our build scripts; the production Docker image runs npm ci --omit=dev. The app itself never parses argv. Should this block the release?
chosen:
Verdict: Secure (for production). vulnerability_count: 0 in the shipped image.
The finding is CVE-2021-44906 / GHSA-xvch-5gv4-984h (CWE-1321), which does affect minimist 1.2.5 (fixed in 1.2.6). But exploitation needs attacker-controlled arguments passed to minimist, and here it only parses arguments written by your own build scripts and is excluded from the runtime image by --omit=dev. Not a release blocker; bump it in the dev tree when convenient (npm audit fix or an override to >=1.2.6).
rejected:
Verdict: Insecure. vulnerability_count: 1.
CVE-2021-44906 / GHSA-xvch-5gv4-984h is rated critical (CWE-1321) and minimist 1.2.5 is inside the affected range, so the build is vulnerable to prototype pollution. Critical advisories should block a release regardless of where the dependency sits in the tree. Upgrade minimist to 1.2.6 through an npm override before shipping and re-run npm audit until it is clean.
author: claude-draft

flaw_note: believes 2.15.0 closed Log4Shell completely; CVE-2021-45046 still affects 2.15.0
prompt: A legacy Java service logs request headers with a pattern layout that uses Thread Context lookups (${ctx:userAgent}). It was upgraded to log4j-core 2.15.0 in December 2021. Is it still exposed to the Log4Shell family?
chosen: Verdict: Insecure. vulnerability_count: 1. 2.15.0 fixes CVE-2021-44228 (affected 2.13.0 up to 2.15.0), but the fix was incomplete: CVE-2021-45046 / GHSA-7rjr-3q55-vv33 (critical) affects 2.13.0 up to but not including 2.16.0, and is exploitable precisely when a pattern layout uses Context Lookups such as ${ctx:...} over attacker-controlled data like a User-Agent. Upgrade log4j-core to 2.17.1 or later (Java 8) and remove ctx lookups on untrusted values.
rejected: Verdict: Secure. vulnerability_count: 0. log4j-core 2.15.0 is the release that fixed Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228 / GHSA-jfh8-c2jp-5v3q): it disables JNDI lookups by default and limits LDAP to localhost. Because the service runs 2.15.0, attacker-supplied headers can no longer trigger remote lookups, and the ctx pattern simply prints the stored value. No further upgrade is required.
author: claude-draft

flaw_note: right advisory but calls a critical unauthenticated RCE a low-severity info leak
prompt: Inventory scan of a vendor appliance shows log4j-core-2.14.1.jar on the classpath of its public-facing login service, which logs failed usernames. Classify the risk for our weekly vulnerability report.
chosen:
- Verdict: Insecure
- vulnerability_count: 1
- Issue: CVE-2021-44228 / GHSA-jfh8-c2jp-5v3q (Log4Shell), critical; CWE-917 / CWE-502
- 2.14.1 is in the affected range (2.13.0 to before 2.15.0). Logging attacker-chosen usernames on an internet-facing login is the classic trigger: a ${jndi:ldap://...} string can lead to unauthenticated remote code execution.
- Report as critical with emergency priority; patch to 2.17.1+ or ask the vendor for a fixed build, and isolate the service meanwhile.
rejected:
- Verdict: Needs changes
- vulnerability_count: 1
- Issue: CVE-2021-44228 / GHSA-jfh8-c2jp-5v3q, low severity; CWE-532 (sensitive data in log files)
- The service writes failed usernames to its logs, which may expose personal data to anyone with log access.
- Report as low priority; schedule an upgrade with the vendor's next maintenance release and restrict log file permissions.
author: claude-draft

flaw_note: catches only the cosmetic issue and misses the axios XSRF-TOKEN leak that the config enables
chosen: {"verdict": "Insecure", "vulnerability_count": 2, "issues": ["CVE-2023-45857 / GHSA-wf5p-g6vw-rhxx (CWE-352, moderate)", "CWE-400: timeout 0 (no request timeout)"], "summary": "axios 1.0.0 to before 1.6.0 sends the X-XSRF-TOKEN header (read from the XSRF-TOKEN cookie) on every request, including cross-origin ones, so the partner beacon host receives your CSRF token. Upgrade to axios>=1.6.0 and use a separate instance without withCredentials for third-party calls; also set a finite timeout."}
rejected: {"verdict": "Needs changes", "vulnerability_count": 1, "issues": ["CWE-400: timeout 0 (no request timeout)"], "summary": "timeout: 0 disables the request timeout, so a slow upstream can hold connections open and exhaust browser sockets. Set a finite timeout such as 10000 ms. withCredentials only attaches cookies to same-site requests, so third-party calls do not expose session data."}
author: claude-draft

flaw_note: flags urllib3 1.26.18 although the 1.x fix landed in 1.26.17
prompt: Scanner says our image is exposed to the urllib3 Cookie-header-on-redirect bug. pip freeze shows urllib3==1.26.18 (we are stuck on 1.26.x because of botocore). Is that a true positive?
chosen: Verdict: Secure (false positive for that advisory). vulnerability_count: 0. The Cookie-header leak on cross-origin redirects is CVE-2023-43804 / GHSA-v845-jxx5-vc9f (CWE-200). On the 1.x line it affects versions before 1.26.17, and on 2.x it affects 2.0.0 up to 2.0.6. 1.26.18 is after the 1.26.17 fix, so the finding does not apply; check that the scanner is reading the installed version and not an older wheel cached in the image.
rejected: Verdict: Needs changes. vulnerability_count: 1. CVE-2023-43804 / GHSA-v845-jxx5-vc9f (high) is valid here: the Cookie stripping fix was only released on the 2.x branch (2.0.6), and the 1.26.x line never received a backport. Staying on 1.26.18 for botocore keeps the leak; strip Cookie manually before following redirects, or move to urllib3 2.0.6 and pin a newer botocore.
author: claude-draft

flaw_note: recommends upgrading to 3.1.3, which only fixed the space case; the follow-up CVE-2024-34064 needs 3.1.4
prompt:
Template code (Jinja2 3.1.2):

<div {{ user_attrs|xmlattr }}>

user_attrs is a dict built from query parameters, keys included. What is the issue and which upgrade fixes it?
chosen: Verdict: Insecure. vulnerability_count: 1. The xmlattr filter on Jinja2 3.1.2 accepts keys containing spaces, so a user-chosen key can inject extra attributes such as onmouseover=... (CVE-2024-22195 / GHSA-h5c8-rqwp-cp95, CWE-79). 3.1.3 rejected spaces but the fix was incomplete: keys with /, >, or = still inject (CVE-2024-34064 / GHSA-h75v-3vvj-5mfj), fixed in 3.1.4. Upgrade to jinja2>=3.1.4, and never let request data choose attribute names; allow-list the keys instead.
rejected: Verdict: Needs changes. vulnerability_count: 1. The xmlattr filter on Jinja2 3.1.2 accepts keys containing spaces, so a user-chosen key can inject event-handler attributes (CVE-2024-22195 / GHSA-h5c8-rqwp-cp95, CWE-79). The maintainers fixed this in 3.1.3 by rejecting keys that contain whitespace. Upgrade to jinja2==3.1.3 and the filter becomes safe for request-supplied dictionaries, keys included.
author: claude-draft

flaw_note: confidently clears ImageMath.eval with a user-controlled environment on Pillow<10.2.0
prompt:
Image service, Pillow 10.0.1. A 'custom filter' feature lets users submit an expression and named parameters:

from PIL import ImageMath
out = ImageMath.eval(req['expr'], **{'a': img, **req['params']})

We already block __ in expr. Safe to ship?
chosen:
- Verdict: Insecure
- vulnerability_count: 1
- Issue: CVE-2023-50447 / GHSA-3f63-hfp8-52jq (CWE-94/95), critical
- Pillow before 10.2.0 lets the keys of the environment argument to ImageMath.eval reach the evaluator, so attacker-chosen parameter names can execute arbitrary code; filtering __ in expr does not cover the environment.
- Fix: pillow>=10.2.0, never pass user-controlled names into the environment, and replace free-form expressions with a fixed menu of filters.
rejected:
- Verdict: Secure
- vulnerability_count: 0
- Issue: none
- ImageMath.eval runs expressions in a restricted namespace that only exposes image operators, and blocking __ in the expression prevents access to builtins and dunder attributes.
- Parameters are passed as plain values, so they cannot introduce code.
- Safe to ship as written; consider logging submitted expressions for monitoring.
author: claude-draft

flaw_note: fields contradict: two issues listed but count 0, verdict Insecure for a moderate open redirect
chosen: {"verdict": "Needs changes", "vulnerability_count": 2, "issues": ["CWE-601: open redirect, startsWith('/') accepts protocol-relative //evil.example", "CVE-2024-29041 / GHSA-rv95-896h-c2vc (moderate): express <4.19.2 open redirect with malformed URLs in res.location/res.redirect"], "summary": "A next value of //evil.example passes the check and redirects off-site, and Express 4.18.2 is also in the range of the malformed-URL redirect advisory. Upgrade to express>=4.19.2 and validate next against an allow-list of internal paths (reject // and backslashes)."}
rejected: {"verdict": "Insecure", "vulnerability_count": 0, "issues": ["CWE-601: open redirect via protocol-relative //evil.example", "CVE-2024-29041 / GHSA-rv95-896h-c2vc: express <4.19.2 malformed URL redirect"], "summary": "The startsWith('/') check lets //evil.example through, and Express 4.18.2 has the malformed-URL redirect advisory. Upgrade express and restrict next to known paths."}
author: claude-draft

flaw_note: ignores that the ranges are hard-coded constants, so the ReDoS input is not attacker-controlled
chosen: Verdict: Secure (not exploitable here). vulnerability_count: 0. The advisory is CVE-2022-25883 / GHSA-c2qf-rxjj-qqgw (CWE-1333): new Range() in semver 7.0.0 to before 7.5.2 can backtrack catastrophically on crafted range strings. Your only range is a hard-coded literal and the version comes from the runtime, so no attacker can supply the slow input. No emergency patch; take semver>=7.5.2 in the next routine dependency update.
rejected: Verdict: Insecure. vulnerability_count: 1. CVE-2022-25883 / GHSA-c2qf-rxjj-qqgw is a high-severity ReDoS in semver 7.0.0 to before 7.5.2, and 7.5.1 is in range. satisfies() builds a Range internally, so every call runs the vulnerable regular expression and the CLI can be hung. Treat it as urgent: upgrade semver to 7.5.2 immediately and add a timeout around version checks.
author: claude-draft

flaw_note: reports a minor header issue and misses the debugger enabled in a reachable deployment
prompt:
Staging deploy of a Flask app (werkzeug==2.3.7). Our engineers reach it from their laptops over the office VPN:

if __name__ == '__main__':
    app.run(host='0.0.0.0', port=8080, debug=True)

Responses also lack an X-Content-Type-Options header. Review please.
chosen:
- Verdict: Insecure
- vulnerability_count: 2
- Issues: CVE-2024-34069 / GHSA-2g68-c3qc-8985 (high); CWE-489 (debug mode exposed); missing X-Content-Type-Options (low)
- debug=True on 0.0.0.0 exposes the Werkzeug interactive debugger, which runs arbitrary Python. Werkzeug before 3.0.3 also lets a malicious site the engineer visits drive the debugger on a reachable host, so the PIN is not a sufficient barrier.
- Fix: never run debug in shared environments; werkzeug>=3.0.3; serve with gunicorn; add nosniff as a minor hardening item.
rejected:
- Verdict: Needs changes
- vulnerability_count: 1
- Issues: missing X-Content-Type-Options (CWE-693, low)
- Without nosniff, browsers may MIME-sniff responses and render uploaded files as HTML.
- debug=True is fine on staging because the Werkzeug debugger is protected by a PIN and the host is only reachable over VPN.
- Fix: add X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff via an after_request hook.
author: claude-draft

flaw_note: proposes an upgrade target that is still inside the affected range (2.6.6 < 2.6.7)
prompt: Our Node 16 webhook relay uses node-fetch 2.6.1 to call customer URLs with our Authorization: Bearer header and follows redirects by default. Which upgrade fixes the credential-forwarding issue?
chosen: Verdict: Insecure. vulnerability_count: 1. node-fetch before 2.6.7 (and 3.0.0 to 3.1.0) forwards sensitive headers such as Authorization and Cookie when following a redirect to a different host (CVE-2022-0235 / GHSA-r683-j2x4-v87g, high). A customer URL that redirects elsewhere hands your bearer token to that third party. Upgrade to node-fetch>=2.6.7 (or >=3.1.1), and set redirect: 'manual' for customer-controlled URLs so you decide what to follow.
rejected: Verdict: Insecure. vulnerability_count: 1. node-fetch 2.6.1 forwards sensitive headers such as Authorization and Cookie when following a redirect to a different host (CVE-2022-0235 / GHSA-r683-j2x4-v87g, high). A customer URL that redirects elsewhere hands your bearer token to that third party. Upgrade to node-fetch 2.6.6, the release that added cross-host header stripping, and keep the default redirect behaviour.
author: claude-draft

flaw_note: says only ws 8.x is affected; 7.0.0 to <7.5.10 is also affected, so 7.5.9 is vulnerable
prompt: Public WebSocket gateway, Node 18, ws@7.5.9 (we cannot move to ws 8 yet). The upgrade request headers come straight from the internet. Any known DoS advisory? Reply as SECURITY_REVIEW JSON.
chosen: {"verdict": "Insecure", "vulnerability_count": 1, "issues": ["CVE-2024-37890 / GHSA-3h5v-q93c-6h6q (high)"], "summary": "A request with more headers than server.maxHeadersCount can crash a ws server (NULL dereference, CWE-476). The fix was backported: ws 7.x is affected before 7.5.10, so 7.5.9 is vulnerable on an internet-facing gateway. Upgrade to ws@7.5.10 (no major bump needed), or as a stopgap reduce --max-http-header-size and set server.maxHeadersCount to 0."}
rejected: {"verdict": "Secure", "vulnerability_count": 0, "issues": [], "summary": "The many-headers crash (CVE-2024-37890) was introduced in the ws 8 rewrite of the upgrade handler and only affects 8.0.0 to 8.17.0. The 7.x branch uses the older parser and is not affected, so ws@7.5.9 is fine for an internet-facing gateway; keep Node's default header limits."}

flaw_note: claims WAR on Tomcat is the safe deployment; it is the documented exploitable one
prompt: Inherited Java app: Spring Boot 2.6.3 (spring-webmvc 5.3.15), JDK 11, packaged as a WAR and deployed on Tomcat 9. Controllers bind form posts to POJOs with @ModelAttribute. A colleague says Spring4Shell only hits executable JARs. Who is right?
chosen: Verdict: Insecure. vulnerability_count: 1. Your colleague has it backwards. CVE-2022-22965 / GHSA-36p3-wjmg-h94x (Spring4Shell, critical) affects spring-beans/webmvc 5.3.0 to before 5.3.18 on JDK 9+, and the publicly documented exploit needs exactly a WAR on Tomcat with data binding to POJOs. Spring Boot executable JARs were not shown exploitable by that path. Upgrade to Spring Boot 2.6.6+ (Framework 5.3.18+), or as a stopgap set disallowed fields such as class.* on the WebDataBinder.
rejected: Verdict: Secure. vulnerability_count: 0. Your colleague is right. CVE-2022-22965 / GHSA-36p3-wjmg-h94x (critical) relies on the class loader of Spring Boot's embedded Tomcat in an executable JAR; standalone Tomcat isolates web application class loaders, so a WAR deployment does not expose the vulnerable property path. With JDK 11 and a WAR on Tomcat 9 no change is needed, although upgrading at the next release is good hygiene.
author: claude-draft

flaw_note: cites a withdrawn advisory as a live critical RCE in jwt.verify
prompt:
Audit question: our API verifies tokens with jsonwebtoken 9.0.2:

jwt.verify(token, process.env.JWT_PUBLIC_KEY, { algorithms: ['RS256'] })

The key comes from our secret manager, never from the request. Is there a live RCE advisory against this usage?
chosen:
- Verdict: Secure (for the code shown)
- vulnerability_count: 0
- The RCE-style report people cite for jwt.verify, CVE-2022-23529 / GHSA-27h2-hvpr-p74q, was withdrawn by GitHub in January 2023 because it required the attacker to control the secretOrPublicKey argument, which is not a realistic threat model.
- Your code pins algorithms to RS256 and loads the key from the secret manager, and 9.0.2 is past the 9.0.0 hardening release.
- Keep the algorithms allow-list; it is what blocks the downgrade issues that were real.
rejected:
- Verdict: Insecure
- vulnerability_count: 1
- Issue: CVE-2022-23529 / GHSA-27h2-hvpr-p74q, critical remote code execution in jwt.verify (CWE-20)
- A crafted token can make jwt.verify execute attacker code during key parsing, and the advisory lists all versions before 9.0.0 plus the 9.0.x line as affected.
- Even with algorithms pinned, the parsing happens before the algorithm check.
- Fix: upgrade to the latest jsonwebtoken and add a WAF rule for oversized tokens.
author: claude-draft
